questions.question: A sum of Rs. 10,500 amounts to Rs. 13,650 in 2 years at a certain rate percent per annum simple interest. The same sum will amount to what in 1 year at the same rate, if the interest is compounded half yearly (nearest to Rs.1)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple Interest in 2 years = 13,650 − 10,500 = ₹3,150

Rate of Interest (R) = (3,150 ÷ 2) ÷ 10,500 × 100 = 15% p.a.

For CI (half-yearly): rate = 7.5% per half-year, periods = 2.

Effective CI rate = 7.5 + 7.5 + (7.5 × 7.5)/100 = 15.5625%.

Total Amount = 10,500 × (100 + 15.5625)% = 10,500 × 1.155625 ≈ ₹12,134.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,134.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹10,500, Amount (SI) = ₹13,650, Time = 2 years.

**Formula:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; CI Amount = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a66a6772d75de2043908d87ce752ff5451572096320a3ad5179e2e5bc856544.png]

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (3,150 × 100) ÷ (10,500 × 2)

⇒ R = 3,15,000 ÷ 21,000 = 15% per annum

⇒ For CI compounded half-yearly for 1 year:

⇒ Rate (r) = 15% ÷ 2 = 7.5% per half-year

⇒ Time (n) = 1 × 2 = 2 half-years

⇒ Amount = 10,500 × (1 + 7.5/100)²

⇒ Amount = 10,500 × (1.075)²

⇒ Amount = 10,500 × 1.155625

⇒ Amount = 12,134.0625 ≈ ₹12,134

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,134.**

Effective Rate for Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time is doubled (2T). The effective rate for two periods is x + y + (xy/100)%.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years (or 2 compounding cycles), the difference between CI and SI is given by P(R/100)².

questions.question: What is the value of (2)/(1 times 3) + (2)/(3 times 5) + (2)/(5 times 7) + .... (2)/(99 times 101) ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Series: 2 / (1 × 3) + 2 / (3 × 5) + 2 / (5 × 7) + ... + 2 / (99 × 101)

**Formula used:**

The nth term can be written as:

(2)/([(2n - 1) × (2n + 1)])

**Calculations:**

Decompose the general term using partial fractions:

(2)/((2n - 1) × (2n + 1)) = (A)/((2n - 1) + B / (2n + 1))

Thus, 2 = A × (2n + 1) + B × (2n - 1)

Comparing coefficients:

A + B = 0

A - B = 2

Solving these:

A = 1

B = -1

Therefore:

(2)/((2n - 1) × (2n + 1)) = 1 / (2n - 1) - 1 / (2n + 1)

The series becomes:

(1 / 1 - 1 / 3) + (1 / 3 - 1 / 5) + (1 / 5 - 1 / 7) + ... + (1 / 99 - 1 / 101)

The sum is: 1 - (1)/(101)

∴ The value of the series is (100)/(101).

questions.question: After the 11th inning, if the average score is represented by 'x', and if in the 12th inning, he scores 84 runs, thereby increasing his average by 4 runs, what is the new average score for the 12th inning?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net increase in total runs = Total innings × Increase in average = 12 × 4 = 48 runs.

The extra runs above the old average scored in the 12th inning = 48 runs.

Old average (after 11 innings) = Runs scored in 12th inning − Net increase = 84 − 48 = 36.

New average (after 12 innings) = Old average + 4 = 36 + 4 = 40 runs.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/814e2be01e498239fe742c1d4d054676ffe96bad957e0601652eb4f8e8a9807a.png] 

**Given:**

Average score after 11 innings = x

Runs scored in the 12th inning = 84

Increase in average = 4 runs

New average after 12 innings = x + 4

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = Average × Number of observations

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total runs after 11 innings = 11 × x = 11x

⇒ Total runs after 12 innings = 11x + 84

⇒ Since the new average is (x + 4), total runs after 12 innings = 12 × (x + 4)

⇒ Equating both total runs expressions:

⇒ 11x + 84 = 12(x + 4)

⇒ 11x + 84 = 12x + 48

⇒ 12x − 11x = 84 − 48

⇒ x = 36

⇒ The old average (after 11 innings) is 36.

⇒ New average for the 12th inning = x + 4 = 36 + 4 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Combined Average

If group A has average A₁ with N₁ items and group B has average A₂ with N₂ items, the combined average is (N₁A₁ + N₂A₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂).

Net Deviation Method

When a new observation is added, the total change in average is completely defined by how much the new value deviates from the previous average. This is useful to mentally calculate averages without large numbers.

questions.question: A single narrative detailing one of Buddha's former existences is known by which of the following names?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Jataka tales** are a collection of stories that recount the former lives of Gautama Buddha, including his incarnations as animals, humans, and divine beings.
 
• These narratives illustrate moral lessons and ethical principles, often emphasizing virtues such as compassion, generosity, and wisdom.
 
• Jataka stories are part of the Pali Canon (Tipitaka), specifically within the Khuddaka Nikaya of the Sutta Pitaka, making them an integral part of Buddhist literature.
 
• There are approximately **547 Jataka tales**, each showcasing a unique aspect of Buddha's journey toward enlightenment.
 
• These tales are widely popular in Buddhist traditions and have influenced art, literature, and folklore across Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vinaya:** Refers to the monastic code and rules of discipline for Buddhist monks and nuns. It forms part of the Tipitaka, the sacred Buddhist scriptures.
 
• **Tripitaka:** The "Three Baskets," comprising the Vinaya Pitaka (discipline), Sutta Pitaka (teachings), and Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophy), which are the foundational texts of Theravada Buddhism.
 
• **Sutra:** A term used for Buddhist discourses or teachings, often delivered by Buddha or his disciples; they are central to Mahayana and other Buddhist traditions.
 
• **Jataka Art:** Jataka tales have been depicted in ancient Indian art, particularly in murals and carvings at sites like Ajanta and Sanchi, symbolizing the spread of Buddhist teachings through visual storytelling.
 
• **Buddhist Literature:** The Jataka tales, along with other Buddhist texts, have played a crucial role in preserving the history and ethical framework of Buddhism across centuries.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution explicitly declares laws violating Fundamental Rights as void?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 13**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 13** of the Indian Constitution explicitly declares that any law inconsistent with or violating Fundamental Rights shall be void.
 
• This Article ensures that Fundamental Rights, enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, remain supreme and protected from legislative infringement.
 
• It provides for judicial review, empowering courts to strike down laws that violate Fundamental Rights.
 
• Article 13 classifies laws into two categories: pre-Constitution laws (existing laws before January 26, 1950) and post-Constitution laws.
 
• The judiciary plays a crucial role in interpreting Article 13 to ensure the protection of Fundamental Rights, making it a cornerstone of India's constitutional framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights** are basic rights guaranteed to all citizens under Part III of the Indian Constitution, ensuring equality, freedom, and protection against arbitrary actions of the state.
 
• **Judicial Review:** A process through which courts assess the validity of laws and executive actions to ensure compliance with the Constitution.
 
• **Doctrine of Eclipse:** Under Article 13, pre-Constitution laws conflicting with Fundamental Rights are not nullified but remain dormant, becoming enforceable if the conflict is removed later.
 
• **Doctrine of Severability:** If a part of a law violates Fundamental Rights, only the offending portion is declared invalid, and the rest remains operational.
 
• **Article 32:** Known as the "Right to Constitutional Remedies," it empowers citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly to enforce Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Which body primarily exercises the powers delegated through Article 243W of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Municipal Corporations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 243W of the Indian Constitution provides for the **functional responsibilities and powers** of **Municipalities**, which include **Municipal Corporations**, **Municipal Councils**, and **Nagar Panchayats**.
 
• The article is part of the **74th Constitutional Amendment Act**, which introduced the concept of urban local governance in India.
 
• The functions under Article 243W include the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice, implementation of schemes, and responsibilities related to **urban infrastructure and services**, such as water supply, sanitation, and urban planning.
 
• **Municipal Corporations** are established in larger cities and are responsible for urban development, governance, and providing essential services such as **roads, education, health care, waste management, and street lighting.**
 
• The powers and responsibilities delegated to Municipal Corporations are outlined in the **12th Schedule** of the Constitution, which includes **18 functional areas**, such as urban planning, regulation of land use, slum improvement, public health, and more.
 
• The **State Legislature** is responsible for defining the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities under Article 243W.
 
• Municipal Corporations ensure the implementation of policies and schemes at the urban level, contributing to **decentralized governance** as envisaged by the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parliament of India**__

 __
 
• The **Parliament of India** is the supreme legislative body in the country and consists of the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• Its role is to enact laws and policies, including constitutional amendments such as the **73rd and 74th Amendments**, which introduced Panchayati Raj and urban local bodies.
 
• While the Parliament provides a framework for governance, it does not directly exercise powers under Article 243W; these are delegated to urban local bodies like Municipal Corporations.
 
 
 
• **Panchayati Raj Institutions**__
 __
 
• **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)** are responsible for rural governance and exercise powers under **Article 243G**, not Article 243W.
 
• PRIs operate at three levels: **Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti,** and **Zila Parishad**, focusing on rural development and decentralized governance.
 
• They handle functions related to **agriculture, rural infrastructure, and poverty alleviation**, as outlined in the **11th Schedule** of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **State Legislature**__
 
 
• The **State Legislature** plays a critical role in defining the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipal Corporations and other urban local bodies under Article 243W.
 
• It establishes laws and frameworks for governance at the urban level, including the enactment of state-specific **Municipal Acts**.
 
• However, it does not directly exercise the powers delegated under Article 243W; it delegates these to the urban local bodies.

• **Article 243V:**

 
 
• Article 243V of the Indian Constitution specifically details the provisions regarding the **disqualification for membership of a Municipality**.
 
• It states that a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of a Municipality if they are disqualified by any law for the time being in force for the purposes of elections to the Legislature of the State concerned.
 
• An important clause under this article is that no person shall be disqualified on the ground that he is less than twenty-five years of age, if he has attained the **age of twenty-one years**.
 
• If any question arises as to whether a member of a Municipality has become subject to any of the disqualifications, the question shall be referred for the decision of such authority and in such manner as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Panchayats:**

 
 
• Disqualifications for membership in Panchayats are governed by **Article 243F** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Similar to Article 243V, it stipulates that the minimum age for eligibility is 21 years and refers other disqualification criteria to state laws.
 
• Panchayats fall under Part IX of the Constitution, which was added by the 73rd Amendment Act.
 
 
 
• **State Legislature:**
 
 
• Disqualifications for members of the State Legislative Assembly or Council are dealt with under **Article 191**.
 
• Common grounds include holding an office of profit, being of unsound mind, being an undischarged insolvent, or not being a citizen of India.
 
 
 
• **District Council:**
 
 
• District Councils generally refer to bodies in autonomous districts under the **Sixth Schedule** of the Constitution or the Zila Parishads in the Panchayati Raj system.
 
• The disqualification rules for Sixth Schedule District Councils are defined by the rules made by the Governor or the Council itself under the provisions of the Sixth Schedule, rather than Article 243V.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• Article 243V is part of **Part IX-A** of the Constitution, which deals with "The Municipalities."
 
• This part was inserted into the Constitution by the **74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**.
 
• The 74th Amendment Act came into force on **June 1, 1993**, aimed at strengthening Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and giving them constitutional status.
 
• Under this framework, three types of Municipalities are provided: Nagar Panchayats for transitional areas, Municipal Councils for smaller urban areas, and Municipal Corporations for larger urban areas.

questions.question:
Which of the following are mechanically formed Sedimentary rocks?

1. Sandstone

2. Loess

3. Halite

4. Chert

5. Geyserite

6. Conglomerate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4: 1, 2, and 6 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mechanically formed sedimentary rocks** are created through the physical accumulation and compaction of sediments, such as sand, gravel, and silt.
 
• **Sandstone** is a mechanically formed sedimentary rock made from compacted sand grains.
 
• **Loess** is a fine-grained, wind-deposited sedimentary rock formed by the accumulation of silt-sized particles.
 
• **Conglomerate** is a mechanically formed sedimentary rock consisting of rounded pebbles and boulders cemented together.

 

 
• **Depending upon the mode of formation, sedimentary rocks are categorized into three groups:**

 
 
• **Mechanically formed**

 
 
• Eg: Sandstone, conglomerate, limestone, shale, loess, etc.
 
 
 
• **Chemically formed**
 
 
• Eg: Chert, limestone, halite, potash, etc.
 
 
 
• **Organically formed**
 
 
• Eg: Geyserite, chalk, limestone, coal, etc.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mechanically Formed Sedimentary Rocks**: Formed by the physical breakdown and deposition of pre-existing rocks due to erosion, weathering, and transport by agents like rivers, wind, and glaciers.
 
• **Chemically Formed Sedimentary Rocks**: These rocks, such as Halite, form from the evaporation of water, leaving behind mineral deposits.
 
• **Organically Formed Sedimentary Rocks**: Rocks like Chert and Geyserite are formed from the accumulation of biological material, such as silica from microscopic organisms.
 
• **Classification of Sedimentary Rocks**: Based on formation, sedimentary rocks are divided into three types—mechanically formed, chemically formed, and organically formed.
 
• **Importance of Sedimentary Rocks**: These rocks often contain fossils, making them vital for studying Earth's history and are also reservoirs for resources like oil, natural gas, and groundwater.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of space weather events like solar flares and CMEs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alteration of ocean currents**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Space weather events such as solar flares and Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) primarily impact the Earth's magnetosphere and ionosphere, not oceanic systems.
 
• Ocean currents are driven by factors such as wind patterns, Earth's rotation (Coriolis effect), salinity, and temperature gradients, which are unaffected by solar activity.
 
• Space weather influences are limited to electromagnetic interference, high-energy particle radiation, and geomagnetic storms, none of which have direct impacts on ocean currents.
 
• Changes in ocean currents are more closely associated with climate phenomena, like El Niño and La Niña, and tectonic activities rather than external solar or space events.
 
• While space weather can affect technological systems on Earth, it does not have the capability to alter the physical processes governing ocean currents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disruption of satellite communication**
 
 
• Space weather events, such as solar flares and CMEs, release high-energy electromagnetic radiation and charged particles that can disrupt satellite communication systems.
 
• Solar flares can cause radio blackouts, especially in high-frequency (HF) communication systems used for aviation and maritime purposes.
 
• Geomagnetic storms can interfere with satellite positioning systems like GPS, causing errors in navigation and communication services.
 
 
 
• **Blackouts in radio frequencies**
 
 
• Solar flares can emit X-rays and ultraviolet radiation that ionize the Earth's upper atmosphere, disrupting radio wave propagation.
 
• This ionization can lead to signal degradation or complete loss of radio communication over certain frequencies, particularly in the HF band.
 
• Such radio blackouts are often temporary but can have significant impacts on communication and navigation systems.
 
 
 
• **Damage to power grids**
 
 
• Geomagnetic storms caused by CMEs can induce electric currents in power transmission lines, potentially overloading and damaging transformers and other electrical infrastructure.
 
• Major geomagnetic storms in the past, such as the 1989 Quebec blackout, have caused widespread power outages due to geomagnetically induced currents (GICs).
 
• Power grid operators monitor space weather to prepare for potential disruptions and minimize risks.

questions.question: Double taxation relief is provided under __________ of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Chapter IX .'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Double Taxation Relief:**

 
 
• Double taxation occurs when an individual or entity pays tax on the same income in two different jurisdictions. This often happens in cases of international transactions or cross-border investments.
 
• Chapter IX of the Income Tax Act, 1961, specifically deals with provisions to avoid double taxation and provide relief to taxpayers.
 
• Under this chapter, taxpayers can claim relief through either the Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) signed between India and other countries or unilateral relief provided by the Indian tax law.
 
• The objective of these provisions is to ensure that taxpayers are not unfairly burdened and to promote international economic cooperation.
 
• Section 90 and Section 91 of the Income Tax Act govern the implementation of double taxation relief mechanisms.

• This chapter is unrelated to double taxation relief and focuses on the taxation of profits retained by companies instead of distributing them as dividends.
 
 
 
• **Chapter X:**

• It deals with methods to ensure arms-length pricing and prevent tax avoidance but does not cover double taxation relief.
 
 
 
• **Chapter VIII:**

• While it addresses certain reliefs, it does not specifically cover double taxation relief under international tax laws.

questions.question: A low Human Development Index (HDI) score is indicative of ____.

__
 
• The Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite measure that evaluates a country's social and economic development based on three key dimensions: life expectancy, education, and standard of living.
 
• A low HDI score typically indicates poor performance in one or more of these dimensions, especially **low life expectancy**, which signifies inadequate access to healthcare and poor living conditions.
 
• Life expectancy is a critical component of HDI, reflecting the overall health and longevity of a country's population. Low life expectancy often correlates with high infant mortality rates and prevalence of diseases.
 
• Countries with a low HDI score often face challenges such as **poverty, limited healthcare infrastructure, and poor sanitation**, which contribute to lower life expectancy.
 
• UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) publishes HDI reports annually, highlighting disparities in human development across the globe. Countries ranked lower in the HDI typically struggle with issues of inequality and lack of resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The main indicators of the Human Development Index (HDI) are:**

 
 
• Standard of Living: Measured by Gross National Income (GNI) per Capita, adjusted for Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) to reflect material wealth. 
 
• Health: Assessed by Life Expectancy at Birth, indicating a long and healthy life. 
 
• Education: Measured by two factors: Mean Years of Schooling (adults 25+) and Expected Years of Schooling (for children entering school).
 
 
 
• The HDI combines these into a single, composite index to provide a broader picture of development than economic indicators like GDP alone

The Correct answer is __**Gudi Padwa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gudi Padwa** marks the beginning of the **Marathi New Year**.
 
• It is celebrated on the first day of the **Chaitra month** (March-April) as per the **Hindu lunar calendar.**
 
• The festival is mainly observed in the state of **Maharashtra** and some parts of **Goa.**
 
• On this day, a **Gudi** (a bright yellow or saffron cloth adorned with garlands) is hoisted on a bamboo stick, symbolizing **prosperity and victory.**
 
• The festival holds religious and cultural importance as it is also believed to mark the day when **Brahma created the universe.**
 
• Traditional food items like **Puran Poli** and **Shrikhand** are prepared and enjoyed during the celebration.
 
• It is considered an auspicious day for starting new ventures or undertakings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Makar Sankranti**__

 __
 
• **Makar Sankranti** is a harvest festival celebrated across India in the month of January.
 
• It marks the transition of the Sun into the **Capricorn zodiac sign (Makara Rashi)**.
 
• This festival is associated with **kite flying, sesame sweets (tilgul),** and prayers to the Sun God.
 
 
 
• **Ugadi**__
 __
 
• **Ugadi** is celebrated as the **New Year** in the states of **Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh,** and **Telangana.**
 
• It is observed on the first day of the **Chaitra month** as per the Hindu lunar calendar.
 
• The festival involves the preparation of a special dish called **Ugadi Pachadi**, which symbolizes different emotions of life.
 
 
 
• **Pongal**__
 
 
• **Pongal** is a harvest festival celebrated primarily in the state of **Tamil Nadu.**
 
• It is observed in the month of **January** and marks the beginning of the Sun's northward journey (Uttarayan).
 
• A special dish called **Pongal** is prepared using rice, milk, and jaggery during the festival.

Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) The average lifespan of the indigenous flora found in the high-altitude plateaus / (2) is significantly longer than that of the lowland varieties, / (3) which are often subjected to more frequent parasitic infestations / (4) and extreme fluctuating in soil acidity and moisture levels.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. and extreme fluctuating in soil acidity and moisture levels .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"and extreme fluctuating"** contains an error in grammatical structure. The word **"fluctuating"** is a present participle (verb form), but it is incorrectly paired with the adjective **"extreme."**
 
• The correct form should use a noun instead of the participle. For example, **"extreme fluctuations"** would be grammatically accurate.
 
• Hence, the revised sentence should read: **"and extreme fluctuations in soil acidity and moisture levels."**

Correct sentence: *The average lifespan of the indigenous flora found in the high-altitude plateaus is significantly longer than that of the lowland varieties, which are often subjected to more frequent parasitic infestations and extreme **fluctuations** in soil acidity and moisture levels.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Grammar Error:**

 
 
• **Incorrect pairing:** Adjectives like "extreme" should pair with nouns, not participles.
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: "extreme fluctuating temperatures." Correct: "extreme fluctuations in temperatures."
 
 
 
• **Usage of Nouns:**
 
 
• Nouns like "fluctuations" are used to describe measurable changes or variations.
 
• In scientific contexts, precision in language is critical for clarity.

Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) The international tribunal has issued a formal demand that the regime / (2) ceases its state-sponsored suppression of political dissidents / (3) and allow for a transparent investigation into the alleged / (4) human rights violations committed during the recent civil unrest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. ceases its state-sponsored suppression of political dissidents .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in part 2 of the sentence: **"ceases its state-sponsored suppression of political dissidents."**
 
• The verb **"ceases"** is incorrectly used in the sentence because the demand issued by the international tribunal is in the subjunctive mood.
 
• In formal demands, recommendations, or hypothetical scenarios, the base form of the verb is used after words like "demand," "recommend," or "suggest."
 
• The correct form should be **"cease"** instead of **"ceases."**

Correct sentence: *The international tribunal has issued a formal demand that the regime **cease** its state-sponsored suppression of political dissidents and allow for a transparent investigation into the alleged human rights violations committed during the recent civil unrest.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subjunctive Mood:**

 
 
• Used to express demands, suggestions, wishes, or hypothetical situations.
 
• **Structure:** The base form of the verb is used regardless of the subject.
 
• **Example:** The teacher recommended that the student *study* harder.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Using the incorrect verb form (e.g., adding -s for third-person singular).
 
• Ignoring the subjunctive mood in formal contexts.

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of the** third conditional**, which is used to talk about hypothetical situations in the past.
 
• The structure of the third conditional is **"If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle"**.
 
• In this case, the original sentence correctly follows the third conditional structure:
 
 
• **Condition Clause:** "Had the evidence been presented more clearly during the initial trial" (Past Perfect).
 
• **Result Clause:** "the jury would likely have reached a different verdict" (would have + past participle).
 

Correct sentence: *Had the evidence been presented more clearly during the initial trial, the jury would likely have reached a different verdict regarding the defendant's liability*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1st Conditional Sentence:**

 
 
• **Structure:** If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.
 
• **Usage:** Describes real or possible situations in the future with likely outcomes.
 
 
 
• **2nd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Simple, would + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If I were an astronaut, I would look at the stars all the time.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to unreal or hypothetical present/future situations.
 
 
 
• **3rd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
 
• **Example:** If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to unreal past situations and their imagined outcomes.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What conclusion can be drawn from the author's discussion of "Arctic amplification"?

options.text: Extreme weather events in temperate zones are inextricably linked to the thermal state of the poles.
Mid-latitude weather patterns are becoming more predictable as the jet stream loses its velocity.
The melting of sea ice is a localized event that has little impact on the hydrology of dry tundras.
Human-engineered carbon reductions are the only way to prevent atmospheric blocking.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***A) The connectivity of global weather systems.***

 
 
• The passage explains that Arctic decay is not isolated to the poles. Through "Arctic amplification," the thermal changes in the North impact the mid-latitudes, linking the "thermal state of the poles" directly to weather patterns elsewhere.
 
 
 
• ***B) The role of the Jet Stream as a mediator.***
 
 
• As the temperature difference between the Arctic and mid-latitudes narrows, the jet stream weakens and meanders. This "sluggish" behavior causes weather systems to stall, leading to extreme conditions thousands of miles away.
 
 
 
• ***C) Resultant extreme weather events.***
 
 
• The text explicitly lists "catastrophic droughts" and "unprecedented cold snaps" in temperate regions as consequences of this cryospheric breakdown, proving they are inextricably linked.
 
 

Therefore, the correct conclusion is that **extreme weather events in temperate zones are inextricably linked to the thermal state of the poles (Option 1).**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because a "meandering" and "sluggish" jet stream leads to unpredictable and extreme weather, rather than making patterns more predictable.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because the passage states that the melting of ice wedges fundamentally alters the hydrology of the tundra, turning it into wetlands.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because the author suggests that natural "carbon bombs" might bypass human-engineered reductions, casting doubt on the idea that these reductions are a guaranteed "only way" to prevent the problem.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the primary mechanism by which the "albedo effect" influences planetary temperature?

options.text: By insulating the permafrost from microbial activity through thermal barriers.
By reflecting the majority of solar radiation away from the Earth’s surface.
By accelerating the formation of ice wedges in the underlying terrestrial surfaces.
By stabilizing the carbon potential of the jet stream in the mid-latitudes.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***A) Definition of the Albedo Effect.***

 
 
• The passage describes the cryosphere as a **"planetary radiator."** The albedo effect is the mechanism by which massive ice sheets and sea ice reflect approximately **80% of incoming solar radiation** back into space.
 
 
 
• ***B) Influence on planetary temperature.***
 
 
• By reflecting such a high percentage of solar energy, the ice prevents the Earth from absorbing that heat. When the ice melts, the underlying "dark ocean and terrestrial surfaces" are exposed, which **absorb** rather than reflect energy, leading to further heating.
 
 
 
• ***C) The "Positive Feedback Loop."***
 
 
• The mechanism is a cycle: warming causes ice loss, which lowers the albedo, which leads to more absorption and higher temperatures, further accelerating the melt.
 
 

Therefore, the primary mechanism is **reflecting the majority of solar radiation away from the Earth’s surface (Option 2).**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because thermal insulation is mentioned in the context of **permafrost** soil layers, not as the primary mechanism of the albedo effect.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because the passage states that **melting** ice wedges leads to ground collapse (thermokarst), rather than the albedo effect creating them.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because while the jet stream is affected by the warming Arctic, the albedo effect itself is a surface radiation process, not a stabilizer of "carbon potential."

questions.question: Which of the following best identifies the central thesis of the passage?

options.text: The logistical challenges of measuring methane clathrates in high-latitude thermokarst lakes.
The role of the Arctic as a passive indicator of global industrial pollution levels.
The transition of the cryosphere from a climate stabilizer to an active, self-reinforcing driver of global warming.
The historical evolution of the jet stream in response to various solar insolation cycles.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***A) The Arctic is a "primary driver" of climatic momentum rather than a passive indicator.***

 
 
• The passage refutes the "canary in the coal mine" metaphor, arguing that the cryosphere is transitioning from a **stabilizer** (planetary radiator) to an **active driver** through positive feedback loops.
 
 
 
• ***B) The Albedo Effect and Permafrost create self-sustaining warming cycles.***
 
 
• The text explains how melting ice exposes dark surfaces that absorb more heat (albedo feedback) and how thawing permafrost releases "carbon bombs" (methane and CO2). These processes create cycles that become **independent of human industrial activity**.
 
 
 
• ***C) Arctic decay has global consequences through "Arctic amplification."***
 
 
• The weakening temperature gradient disrupts the jet stream, causing "atmospheric blocking" and extreme weather thousands of miles away. This reinforces the idea of the Arctic as a central, active force in the global climate system.
 
 

Therefore, the central thesis is the **transition of the cryosphere from a climate stabilizer to an active, self-reinforcing driver of global warming (Option 3).**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the author explicitly states that the "passive indicator" (canary) metaphor **underestimates** the region's actual role as a driver.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because the jet stream is mentioned as a contemporary consequence of Arctic melting, not as a study of its long-term historical evolution across solar cycles.
